sections.section_title: Section A: Community, Diversity & Our Neighbourhood

questions.instruction: Fill in the blanks with the correct word about neighbourhood places, map symbols, housing, and community living.

items.sentence: A community helper who delivers letters, parcels, and mail to our homes or neighbourhood is called a ________.
On a map, the cardinal direction that always points towards the top is ________.
Houses built with sloping roofs are mostly found in ________ regions so that snow and rainwater slide off easily.
An important place in our neighbourhood where sick or injured people are treated by doctors and nurses is a ________.
Living together in a community teaches us to help each other and share mutual ________ during times of need.

questions.instruction: Choose the correct option for each question based on diversity in lifestyles, housing, landmarks, and community values.

items.question: Why do people living in the desert regions of Rajasthan traditionally wear light cotton clothes and turbans?
options: To protect themselves from heavy snowfall
To keep cool in the hot sun and shield their heads from heat
To protect themselves from floodwaters
Because they only have thick wool available
items.answer: To keep cool in the hot sun and shield their heads from heat

items.question: Which of the following symbols is commonly used on a neighbourhood map to indicate a school nearby?
options: An airplane symbol
An open book or a student walking
A crossed knife and fork
A red plus (+) sign
items.answer: An open book or a student walking

items.question: In Assam, houses are frequently built on raised bamboo pillars called 'stilts'. Why is this house design used?
options: To keep the house safe from heavy rainfall and floods
To make the house look taller than the forest trees
To prevent snow from freezing on the floor
To stop strong winds from blowing the roof away
items.answer: To keep the house safe from heavy rainfall and floods

items.question: Which of the following actions shows a good community value when living together with our neighbours?
options: Throwing garbage in the common corridor
Playing loud music late at night
Helping an elderly neighbour carry their groceries
Refusing to talk to people from other cities
items.answer: Helping an elderly neighbour carry their groceries

items.question: What is a landmark in a neighbourhood?
options: An easily recognisable building or object that helps people find their way
A secret underground tunnel used by vehicles
A temporary toy tent built in a garden
A moving bus or car on the highway
items.answer: An easily recognisable building or object that helps people find their way

questions.instruction: Match each food item to its nutrient group, or each plant to its natural habitat.

pairs.answer: Plants adapted to dry, sandy desert habitats
Aquatic plants growing in ponds and lakes
Protective foods rich in vitamins and minerals

questions.instruction: Identify the odd option out in each group based on healthy habits, eco-friendly practices, and nutrition.

items.question: Identify the UNHEALTHY daily hygiene habit from the following group:
options: Washing hands with soap before eating
Brushing teeth twice every day
Eating food with unwashed hands or unwashed fruits
Bathing daily with clean water
items.answer: Eating food with unwashed hands or unwashed fruits

items.question: Which of the following practices is NOT eco-friendly for conserving our environment?
options: Using cloth or jute bags for shopping
Planting new trees and saplings in the neighbourhood
Burning plastic waste in the open air
Turning off the running tap while brushing teeth
items.answer: Burning plastic waste in the open air

items.question: Pick the odd food item that is considered unhealthy 'junk food' rather than a nutritious dish:
options: Fresh fruit salad
Deep-fried potato chips and sugary soda
Sprouted moong dal chaat
Vegetable khichdi
items.answer: Deep-fried potato chips and sugary soda

items.question: Identify the odd activity that does NOT promote mental well-being and a happy lifestyle:
options: Playing outdoor games with friends
Sleeping for at least 8 hours every night
Staring at mobile screens continuously for 6 hours
Practicing meditation or deep breathing exercises
items.answer: Staring at mobile screens continuously for 6 hours

items.question: Which of these actions harms local plants and trees when you are on a nature trail?
options: Observing fallen leaves on the ground
Plucking flowers and breaking green branches unnecessarily
Watering dry saplings in the garden
Taking photographs of butterflies on flowers
items.answer: Plucking flowers and breaking green branches unnecessarily

sections.section_title: Section C: How Things Work, Materials & Our Sky

questions.instruction: Choose the correct option for questions about simple machines, raw materials, manufacturing, and celestial bodies.

items.question: Which simple machine is used on a flagpost or a well to lift heavy objects easily using a rope and a grooved wheel?
options: Pulley
Inclined plane
Wedge
Screw

items.question: What is the primary natural raw material used by a potter to make earthen pots, diyas, and pitchers?
options: Cotton fibres
Clay
Iron ore
Plastic beads

items.question: Which celestial body is at the centre of our solar system and gives heat and light to the Earth?
options: The Moon
The Sun
The North Star
Planet Mars

items.question: How are cotton fabrics traditionally made from spun cotton threads or yarns?
options: By weaving threads together on a loom
By melting stones in a furnace
By pressing dry leaves together
By boiling sand in water
items.answer: By weaving threads together on a loom

items.question: What causes the daily cycle of Day and Night on Earth?
options: The Sun moving around the Moon
The rotation of the Earth on its own axis
The clouds blocking the stars at night
The Earth moving away from the stars
items.answer: The rotation of the Earth on its own axis

questions.instruction: Answer each question in 1 or 2 English words based on what you learned about how things work, materials, and our sky.

items.question: What do we call a recognizable group or pattern of stars in the night sky, such as the Great Bear (Saptarishi)?
What simple machine is a sloping surface or ramp used to push heavy loads up easily?
Which natural fibre obtained from the fleece of sheep is used to weave warm winter sweaters and blankets?
Which bright star in the northern sky always points towards the North direction and helped ancient travellers navigate?
What do we call the simple machine consisting of a stiff bar that turns on a fixed point (pivot/fulcrum), like a seesaw or crowbar?
